title: Anchor viewport on filter and reload changes
description:
[Spec ref] §4 last bullet (viewport keeps position relative to anchor row when filters change), §8 scroll-to-match centers row.
[Actions]
1. Viewport anchor: on visibility change keep top visible row identity, adjust scrollTop accordingly; table must not jump.
2. Scroll-to-row helper centers a given row in the viewport (used by search, fn filters).
3. Ensure programmatic scrolling never changes horizontal position (§4).
[Acceptance]
- Manual: with a filter toggled, the same anchor row stays at the same viewport position; scroll to row N centers it without horizontal drift.
acceptance_criteria: manual run: no viewport jump on filter change; centered scroll-to-row

title: Virtualized table skeleton
description:
[Spec ref] §4 (columns Line/Time/Category/Message with 50/110/150/600 px defaults and visible headers, pixel scroll, compact rows ~glyph height + 6 px, horizontal scrollbar only when content wider than window, no trackpad horizontal gestures, wheel-tilt horizontal scroll only, scroll preserves horizontal position, type-ahead disabled); §16.
[Actions]
1. Table over @tanstack/react-virtual with fixed row height, absolute pixel scrolling, 6.4M rows from get_rows IPC windows.
2. Columns Line, Time, Category, Message with default widths; headers always visible; user-resizable later is out of scope.
3. Horizontal: scrollbar only when overflow; wheel-tilt scrolls horizontally without changing vertical position; block horizontal touchpad gestures; vertical scroll never changes horizontal offset; scroll-to-row preserves horizontal position.
4. Level colors for whole row text (§3.1) once rows carry level.
5. No built-in type-ahead.
[Acceptance]

acceptance_criteria: manual run on 175 MB file: smooth pixel scroll, correct columns, horizontal rules per §4

title: Core: visibility engine
description:
[Spec ref] §7 combined semantics; §11 counters; §12 pin override.
[Actions]
1. Engine state: filter list with per-filter on/off, level set enabled/disabled, category set enabled/disabled, pin list.
2. visible(i) = (no filters OR text match) AND level_on AND category_on OR pinned (§7 formula), evaluated over an index; produce a visible-rows view (sorted vec of line indexes) recomputed on any change.
3. Counters per level that ignore level toggles: count of rows which become visible if that level is enabled (shown on level buttons, §11).
4. Selection preserved by line number when visibility changes (§4 last bullet).
[Pseudocode]
struct Visibility { filters: Vec<(Matcher, bool)>, levels: EnumMap<Level, bool>, cats: HashSet, pins: Vec<Pin> }
fn recompute(&mut self) -> VisibleView
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests: OR over active filters, no filters = pass, level off hides, category off hides, pin makes hidden row visible, counters ignore level toggles.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core visibility green

title: Core: simple query language
description:
[Spec ref] §6 (grammar OR < AND < NOT, quoted terms, parentheses, case-insensitive keywords), plus span API for §9 highlight rendering.
[Actions]
1. Tokenizer: quoted terms, keywords AND/OR/NOT (case-insensitive), parentheses; everything else = syntax error.
2. Recursive-descent parser: parse(text) -> Result<Query, SyntaxError>; precedence NOT > AND > OR.
3. Evaluator: eval(query, line_text) -> bool (case-insensitive over full line text).
4. Span API: positive_positions(query, line_text) -> Vec<Range> for every occurrence of every positive term (NOT terms excluded) - reused by highlights.
5. Syntax error -> criterion matches nothing; app never panics.
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests for spec examples: error AND timeout; NOT info; (auth OR login) AND failed; precedence a OR b AND c == a OR (b AND c); unclosed quote / empty term / stray symbol -> no match, no panic; multi-occurrence spans correct.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core simple_query green

title: Core: plain, line-number and regex match modes
description:
[Spec ref] §5 (match modes table), §6 not included here (separate task).
[Actions]
1. MatchMode enum { Plain, Regex, Simple, LineNo(u32) }; trait Matcher { fn matches(&self, line_full_text: &str, line_no: u32) -> bool }.
2. Plain: case-insensitive substring (ASCII-lowercase fast path, Unicode fallback).
3. Regex: compile case-insensitive; regex crate fast path, fancy-regex fallback for lookarounds/backreferences (Python-compatible syntax per spec); invalid pattern compiles to NeverMatch, never panics (§5).
4. LineNo: exact 1-based match.
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests: plain CI matching, line number match, regex with (?i)-equivalent behavior, lookbehind pattern works via fancy-regex, invalid regex like ( matches nothing without panic.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core matching plain/regex/lineno green

title: IPC: load result to UI
description:
[Spec ref] §2 (result applied on completion), §4 (Line/Time/Category/Message columns), §16.
[Actions]
1. Tauri command load_file(path) -> LoadResult { format, line_count, categories (tree-ready list with counts), level_counts } executed on a background thread.
2. Tauri command get_rows(req) -> paginated row chunks for the table (visible-range based) so the UI never holds 6.4M parsed rows.
3. Structs derive Serialize and mirror serde types on the TS side with a generated bindings file.
[Acceptance]
- load_file on both test_logs files returns expected format (KSIVA, PLAIN), line counts, category set and 6 levels with counts.
- get_rows serves any window of 1000 rows in < 50 ms on log.txt.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer loading both files; get_rows windows under 50 ms

title: Core: row parsing (formats A/B)
description:
[Spec ref] §3 parse rules and all edge cases; §3.1 level names.
[Actions]
1. Parse into Row { line_no (1-based), time_display (HH:MM:SS.mmm; for format A strip date part before T), category, level, message, raw }.
2. Whitespace separators (sequences of spaces), first field is timestamp.
3. Format A: field 2 = category, field 3 = level candidate. Format B: field 2 (elapsed) discarded, field 3 = level candidate, field 4 = category.
4. Level recognition: long names (LOG_*) and short codes crt/err/wrn/msg/dbg/trc, case-insensitive; unrecognized candidate = MSG level, candidate and rest = message. Missing level = MSG.
5. Categories: missing / single-field = uncategorized; two-field line = uncategorized, MSG, second field is message; empty line = empty message, uncategorized, MSG.
6. Levels enum: CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, MSG, DEBUG, TRACE (§3.1).
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests cover: full A line with and without level tag, full B line, category missing, two-field line, single-field, empty line, multiple-space separators, short and long level codes, unknown level candidate treated as message.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core parsing green; every §3 edge case has a named test

title: Core: scanner - line index and format detection
description:
[Spec ref] §3 (auto-detect two formats by first non-empty line), §16 (hundreds of MB feel instant).
[Actions]
1. Reader over mmap: enumerate line offsets (memchr on b'\n'), build u64 offset index (Vec<u64>).
2. Auto-detect format A (KSIVA) vs B (PLAIN) from first non-empty line; B = 5 fields starting with HH:MM:SS.mmm.
3. Empty/blank-only file handled gracefully (zero rows, empty state stays).
4. Expose: line_count(), raw_line(i) (bytes without trailing newline), detected_format().
[Pseudocode]
struct Scanner { data: Mmap, offsets: Vec<u64> }
fn detect_format(first_line: &[u8]) -> Format
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests with small fixture files written in-test (spec sample lines) for both formats.
- Integration: scan test_logs/log.txt (175 MB) in < 2 s on dev machine; line_count matches wc -l.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core scanner; scan 175 MB log.txt under 2 s both formats detected

title: Open and non-blocking load pipeline
description:
[Spec ref] §2 (Open button, drag-and-drop, non-blocking load, last dir remembered, error handling, empty state swap), §2.1 (Ctrl+R Reload semantics), §14 (Ctrl+C copy deferred to table epic, Ctrl+R here).
[Actions]
1. Open button in bottom bar opens file dialog; remember last dir in app state (settings wire-up later, settings-2).
2. Drag-and-drop on the window: take first dropped file only.
3. Load runs in background thread via core crate; window stays responsive; result applied on completion.
4. Nonexistent file / read error: error message shown, no crash, no data loss.
5. Empty state hidden, table shown after successful load; loading a new file behaves like reload (§2.1): filters kept and re-evaluated, on/off kept, highlights kept, disabled levels and (by name) categories kept, pins cleared, search closed.
6. Reload button + Ctrl+R.
[Pseudocode]
fn open_file(path) { spawn(move || core::load(path)) ; ui shows loading; on result -> store FileState, apply visibility }
[Acceptance]
- Open test_logs/log.txt (175 MB): UI stays responsive during load, rows appear after.
- Open test_logs/TitleId-YBA91-Ksiva-6d865.txt (5.4 MB) loads and detects KSIVA format.
- Drag two files: first one used.
- Open /nonexistent: error message, app alive.
- After filtering, Ctrl+R: filters still active and recomputed.

title: GitHub auto-update (deferred — build the app first)
description: [Context] Owner decision 2026-11-23: update support is LAST priority; the rewrite itself comes first. Decisions agreed so far (variant 2 — full auto-update): [Spec ref] New section of FUNCTIONAL_SPEC.html + edit §1 (replace 'без сетевых функций' with 'единственная сетевая функция — проверка и загрузка обновлений'). [Actions] 1. When the app is functional and GitHub Releases exist, add spec §17 «Обновления». 2. Behavior to spec: source = latest non-prerelease GitHub Release; auto-check at startup at most once per 24h + manual 'Check for updates' (menu + cmdline registry §13); UX: banner 'Update available' with Download / Skip this version / Later, download progress with cancel, then 'Restart to install'; resilience: no network -> silent skip (manual check -> 'Cannot check for updates' message), HTTPS only, signature-verified installer, failed install leaves current version running. 3. Settings §15: 'Automatically check for updates' (on/off), 'Automatically download' (on/off). [Acceptance] Spec section written; behavior matches above; §1 edited.
design: Full auto-update chosen over check-only and hybrid (owner picked 2). Spec stays functional/stack-agnostic; updater library choice (Tauri updater / Sparkle / autoUpdater) belongs to the rewrite. Prerequisite: repo must have GitHub remote + Releases — currently no remote configured.
notes: Owner 2026-11-23: will create the GitHub remote himself later; at that point scope extends to CI release builds + auto-update setup together. Until then this epic stays untouched.
